**Question**

What is the area of the square $ABCD$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of the square $ABCD$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Side of the square}       &= \sqrt {(0 - 4) ^ 2 + (4 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {(-4) ^ 2 + 3 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {16 + 9} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {25} \\\\
                                &= 5 \\\\
\text{Area of the square}       &= \text{(Side of the square)} ^ 2 \\\\
                                &= 5 ^ 2 \\\\
                                &= 25
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the area of the triangle formed by these three points?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of the triangle formed by these three points?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Base of the triangle}     &= \sqrt {(-1 - 2) ^ 2 + (1 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {(-3) ^ 2 + 0 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {9 + 0} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {9} \\\\
                                &= 3 \\\\
\text{Height of the triangle}   &= 2 - 1 \\\\
                                &= 1 \\\\
\text{Area of the square}       &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{(Base of the triangle)} \times \text{(Height of the triangle)} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 3 \times 1 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                &= 1.5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$1.5$

                                &= \sqrt {(-3) ^ 2 + 0 ^ 2} \\\\

                                &= \sqrt {9} \\\\

                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 3 \times 1 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\

**Question**

A square of side length $3 \ \text{cm}$ is divided into three
rectangles of equal size.

The middle rectangle is removed and replaced on the side of the 
original square to form an octagon as shown.

How many times bigger is the perimeter of the octagon than 
the perimeter of the original square?

![papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q35-s02-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q35-s02-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q35-s02-i00.png")

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square of side length $3 \ \text{cm}$ is divided into three
rectangles of equal size.
<emptyline>

original square to form an octagon as shown.
<emptyline>
How many times bigger is the perimeter of the octagon than 
the perimeter of the original square?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>

$\boxed{\text{KEY} \ \ \spadesuit \ 20 \ \text{buses}}$

</div>

The coordinates of $Q$ are $( 30, 50 )$

![papers/city-of-london-school/2008/sample-paper-group-2/s01-q03-s02-i00.png](/assets/papers/city-of-london-school/2008/sample-paper-group-2/s01-q03-s02-i00.png "papers/city-of-london-school/2008/sample-paper-group-2/s01-q03-s02-i00.png")

What are the co-ordinates of points $M$ and $N$? 



</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>

<emptyline>

<emptyline>
What are the co-ordinates of points $M$ and $N$? 
<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

Let the coordinates of M $= (0, b)$

Let the coordinates of N $= (a, 0)$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {0 + a} {2}          &= 30 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2}              &= 30 \\\\
a                           &= 30 \times 2 \\\\
a                           &= 60 \\\\
\dfrac {b + 0} {2}          &= 50 \\\\
\dfrac {b} {2}              &= 50 \\\\
b                           &= 50 \times 2 \\\\
b                           &= 100
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates of M $= (0, 100)$

Coordinates of N $= (60, 0)$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

M is $(0, 100)$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                            &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Students who like pizza}        &= \dfrac {30} {360} \times 48 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {30 \times 48} {360} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {30 \times 12 \times 4} {30 \times 12} \\\\

**Question**

What is the area of the rectangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of the rectangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Length of rectangle}      &= \sqrt {(4 - 4) ^ 2 + (5 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {0 ^ 2 + 4 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {0 + 16} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {16} \\\\
                                &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Breadth of rectangle}     &= \sqrt {(-1 - 4) ^ 2 + (1 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {(-5)) ^ 2 + 0 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {25 + 0} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {25} \\\\
                                &= 5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Area of rectangle}        &= \text{Length of rectangle} \times \text{Breadth of rectangle} \\\\
                                &= 4 \times 5 \\\\
                                &= 20 \ {\text{cm}} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$20$

Show the coordinates of the origin and distance $2, 5, 6$ and $y$


*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 : 5                                           &= 6 : y \\\\
\dfrac {2} {5}                                  &= \dfrac {6} {y} \\\\
2 \times y                                      &= 6 \times 5 \\\\
y                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 5} {2} \\\\
y                                               &= \dfrac {2 \times 3 \times 5} {2} \\\\
y                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 3 \times 5} {\cancel 2} \\\\
y                                               &= 3 \times 5 \\\\
y                                               &= 15
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

                        &= \dfrac {8} {4} \\\\
                        &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I plant some seeds and get three white flowers. Write down how many blue flowers I should expect to grow.

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the expected number of blue flowers $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
1 \ \text{white} : 3 \ \text{blue}              &= 3 \ \text{white} : a \ \text{blue} \\\\
\dfrac{1} {3}                                   &= \dfrac {3} {a} \\\\
1 \times a                                      &= 3 \times 3 \\\\
a                                               &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

Expected number of blue flowers $= 9$

\end{array}
$

Expected number of blue flowers $= 9$

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the expected number of white flowers $= a$

Expected number of pink flowers $= 2a$

Expected number of blue flowers $= 3a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2a + 3a         &= 30 \\\\
6a                  &= 30 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {30} {6} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {6 \times 5} {6} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 5} {\cancel 6} \\\\
a                   &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Expected number of white flowers $= 5$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

= & 6                                                 &:& 1 \\\\
= & 6 \times 5                                        &:& 1 \times 5 \\\\
= & 30                                                &:& 5
\end{array}
$

Expected number of white flowers $= 5$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In another area of the garden, $24$ blue flowers are grown. Calculate how many pink flowers I should expect to find here.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In another area of the garden, $24$ blue flowers are grown. Calculate how many pink flowers I should expect to find here.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the expected number of pink flowers $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \ \text{blue} : 2 \ \text{pink}               &= 24 \ \text{blue} : a \ \text{pink} \\\\
\dfrac{3}{2}                                    &= \dfrac {24} {a} \\\\
3 \times a                                      &= 24 \times 2 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {24 \times 2} {3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {8 \times 3 \times 2} {3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 3 \times 2} {\cancel 3} \\\\
a                                               &= 8 \times 2 \\\\
a                                               &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

Expected number of pink flowers $= 16$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{blue}                               &:& \text{pink} \\\\
= & 3                                         &:& 2 \\\\
= & 3 \times 8                                &:& 2 \times 8 \\\\
= & 24                                        &:& 16
\end{array}
$

Expected number of pink flowers $= 16$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$16$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Height of triangle ABC}   &= 5 - 3 \\\\
                                &= 2 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Base of triangle ABC}     &= 6 - 0 \\\\
                                &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Area of triangle ABC}     &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{Height of triangle ABC} \times \text{Base of triangle ABC} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 2 \times 6 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 6} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 6} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                                &= 6 \ {\text{cm}} ^ 2 \\\\
\text{Area of kite ABCD}        &= 2 \times \text{Area of triangle ABC} \\\\
                                &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
                                &= 12 \ {\text{cm}} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A sheet of graph paper is placed with its $x$-axis pointing due East and its $y$-axis pointing due North. 
A sluggish snail starts at point $(0, 0)$ and slowly, 
but smoothly, slithers $1$ unit North, $2$ units East, $3$ units South, $4$ units West, 
$5$ units North, $6$ units East, $7$ units South, $8$ units West, $9$ units North and (lastly!) $10$ units East. 

At which point does the snail finally arrive? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>

$5$ units North, $6$ units East, $7$ units South, $8$ units West, $9$ units North and (lastly!) $10$ units East. 
<emptyline>

a                                               &= \dfrac {90 \times 18} {100} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {1620} {100} \\\\
a                                               &= 16.2 \ \text{kroner}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 16.2 \ \text{kroner}$

**Question**

How much are $12 \ \text{kroner}$ worth? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How much are $12 \ \text{kroner}$ worth? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the amount of pounds I get $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
18 \ \text{kroner} : \pounds 1                  &= 12 \ \text{kroner} : \pounds a \\\\
18                                              &= \dfrac {12} {a} \\\\
18a                                             &= 12 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {12} {18} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 2} {6 \times 3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 2} {\cancel 6 \times 3} \\\\
a                                               &= \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{kroner}                  &:& \pounds \\\\
= & 18                             &:& 1 \\\\
= & 1                              &:& \dfrac {1} {18} \\\\
= & 1 \times 12                    &:& \dfrac {12} {18} \\\\
= & 12                             &:& \dfrac {6 \times 2} {6 \times 3} \\\\
= & 12                             &:& \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 2} {\cancel 6 \times 3} \\\\
= & 12 \ \text{kroner}             &:& \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}
\end{array}
$

Answer $= \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}$
</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Jo buys some sweets and a magazine that cost $\pounds 5.10$. 
How much is this in kroner?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the value in kroner $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
\pounds 1 : 18 \ \text{kroner}                  &= \pounds 5.1 : a \ \text{kroner} \\\\
\dfrac{1} {18}                                  &= \dfrac {5.1} {a} \\\\
a                                               &= 5.1 \times 18 \\\\
a                                               &= 91.8 \ \text{kroner}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 91.8 \ \text{kroner}$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \pounds                        &:& \text{kroner} \\\\
= & 1                              &:& 18 \\\\
= & 1 \times 5.10                  &:& 18 \times 5.10 \\\\
= & \pounds 5.10                   &:& 91.8 \ \text{kroner}
\end{array}
$

Answer $= 91.8 \ \text{kroner}$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$91.8 \ \text{kroner}$

**Question**

Pembury Youth centre held a Judo club on Tuesday evenings. At the beginning of the year the
children's heights were recorded on a chart. (The last $6$ names are the girls names.)
Complete the chart for the four missing children using the information below.

- If Barry grew another $1 \ \text{cm}$ he would be the same height as the tallest girl.
- Steven is $20 \ \text{cm}$ taller than the shortest boy.

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the difference in height between the shortest member of the club and the tallest member?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the difference in height between the shortest member of the club and the tallest member?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Range} = \text{Highest number} - \text{Lowest number}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Height of Tina}  &= 127 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Height of Faye}  &= 146 - 20 \\\\
                        &= 126 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Height of Barry} &= 137 - 1 \\\\
                        &= 136 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Height of Steven}&= 122 + 20 \\\\
                        &= 142 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Difference}      &= 146 - 113 \\\\
                        &= 33 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$33 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average height of girls}      &= \dfrac {133 + 126 + 113 + 137 + 120 + 127} {6} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {756} {6} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {6 \times 126} {6} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 126} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                                    &= 126 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average height of girls}      &= \dfrac {133 + 126 + 113 + 137 + 120 + 127} {6} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {756} {6} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {6 \times 126} {6} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 126} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                                    &= 126 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

**Working**

Let the total number of boys $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {84} {360} \times a        &= 126 \\\\
a                                 &= 126 \times \dfrac {360} {84} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac {126 \times 360} {84} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac {3 \times 42 \times 2 \times 180} {2 \times 42} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {42} \times \cancel 2 \times 180} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {42}} \\\\
a                                 &= 3 \times 180 \\\\
a                                 &= 540
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of boys with green favourite colour}     &= \dfrac {62} {360} \times 540 \\\\
                                                      &= \dfrac {62 \times 540} {360} \\\\
                                                      &= \dfrac {2 \times 31 \times 3 \times 180} {2 \times 180} \\\\
                                                      &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 31 \times 3 \times \cancel {180}} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {180}} \\\\
                                                      &= 31 \times 3 \\\\
                                                      &= 93
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

= & 126                                         &:& \dfrac {31 \times 2 \times 42 \times 3} {2 \times 42} \\\\
= & 126                                         &:& \dfrac {31 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel {42} \times 3} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {42}} \\\\
= & 126                                         &:& 31 \times 3 \\\\
= & 126                                         &:& 93
\end{array}
$

Number of boys whose favourite is green $= 93$

**Question**

What percentage of pupils travelled had a coach?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{\% of pupils travelled by coach}      &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 100 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {90 \times 100} {360} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 25} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 25} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                            &= 25 \ \%
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

$

How many pupils took a car to school?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="tip">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of people $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}

Let the coordinates $= (a, b)$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1 + a} {2}            &= 7 \\\\
1 + a                         &= 7 \times 2 \\\\
1 + a                         &= 14 \\\\
a                             &= 14 - 1 \\\\
a                             &= 13 \\\\
\dfrac {4 + b} {2}            &= 1 \\\\
4 + b                         &= 1 \times 2 \\\\
4 + b                         &= 2 \\\\
b                             &= 2 - 4 \\\\
b                             &= -2
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (13, -2)$

1 + a                         &= 14 \\\\
a                             &= 14 - 1 \\\\
a                             &= 13 \\\\
\dfrac {4 + b} {2}            &= 1 \\\\
4 + b                         &= 1 \times 2 \\\\
4 + b                         &= 2 \\\\
b                             &= 2 - 4 \\\\
b                             &= -2
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Coordinates $= (13, -2)$
</code></pre>

\end{aligned}

</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

We have to reflect through a vertical line therefore y-coordinates will remain the same,

and x-coordinates of reflected points will be at the same distance as the original points but on the other side

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Distance of point with abscissa 3}    &= 20 - 3 \\\\
                                              &= 17 \\\\
\text{Corresponding reflected abscissa}       &= 20 + 17 \\\\
                                              &= 37 \\\\
\text{Distance of point with abscissa 5}    &= 20 - 5 \\\\
                                              &= 15 \\\\
\text{Corresponding reflected abscissa}       &= 20 + 15 \\\\
                                              &= 35
\end{aligned}
$

$(35, 3), (37, 3), (35, 5), (37, 5)$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

                              &= 4
\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

![papers/st-georges-college/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q19-i00.png](/assets/papers/st-georges-college/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q19-i00.png "papers/st-georges-college/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q19-i00.png")

The pie chart shows the proportions of different colours of cars in a school carpark. There were $36$ black cars. How many blue cars were there?   

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>
The pie chart shows the proportions of different colours of cars in a school carpark. There were $36$ black cars. How many blue cars were there?   
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{black}                             &:& \text{blue} \\\\
= & 40 \%                                    &:& 30 \% \\\\
= & 1                                        &:& \dfrac {30} {40} \\\\
= & 1 \times 36                              &:& \dfrac {30 \times 36} {40} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& \dfrac {3 \times 10 \times 4 \times 9} {4 \times 10} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel 4 \times 9} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {10}} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& 3 \times 9 \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& 27
\end{array}
$

Number of blue cars $= 36$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36$

</div>

**Question**

The chart below shows the mileage between five places in North London. For example it gives the distance between Kenton and 
Hampstead as $4 \ \text{miles}$.

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q16-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q16-i00.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q16-i00.png")

She then visits her sister in Harpenden before driving home via Habs. How far does she travel altogether?

\begin{aligned}
\text{Amount of water flowing per minute}   &= \dfrac {1000} {5} \\\\

                                            &= 200 \ \text{litres}
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Amount of water flowing per minute}   &= \dfrac {1000} {5} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5 \times 200} {5} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 200} {\cancel 5} \\\\
                                            &= 200 \ \text{litres}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

**Question**

The y-coordinate of the centre of one of the squares in this sequence is $2177$. Work out the x-coordinate of this square.

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q28-s05-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q28-s05-i00.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q28-s05-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The y-coordinate of the centre of one of the squares in this sequence is $2177$. Work out the x-coordinate of this square.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the x-coordinate $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a - 1      &= 2177 \\\\
2a - 1              &= 2177 \\\\
2a                  &= 2177 + 1 \\\\
2a                  &= 2178 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {2178} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 1089} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 1089} {\cancel 2} \\\\
a                   &= 1089
\end{aligned}
$

X-coordinate of the center of the square $= 1089$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

= & 45                                      &:& \dfrac {\cancel {12} \times 15 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel {12} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
= & 45                                      &:& 15
\end{array}
$

Number of people who choose $= 15$

**Question**

The average rainfall for the first three months of the year is

$\dfrac{50 + 40 + 35}{3} = \dfrac{125}{3} = 41 \dfrac{2}{3} \ \text{mm}$

Work out the average rainfall for the last three months. Give your answer as a mixed fraction.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

<emptyline>

</code></pre>
</div>

\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

Peter buys $1500$ shares in $2009$ and sells them in a later year. Given that he makes a loss of $\pounds 3000$, 
find the two possible years in which he might have sold his shares.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Peter buys $1500$ shares in $2009$ and sells them in a later year. Given that he makes a loss of $\pounds 3000$, 
find the two possible years in which he might have sold his shares.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Loss per share}       &= \dfrac {3000} {1500} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {1500 \times 2} {1500} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {\cancel {1500} \times 2} {\cancel {1500}} \\\\
                              &= \pounds 2 \\\\
\text{Selling price of share} &= 6 - 2\\\\
                              &= \pounds 4
\end{aligned}
$

Two possible years $= 2010, 2014$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$2010, 2014$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Angle of Mathematics sector}  &= 33 \dfrac {1} {3} \% \ \text{of} \ 360 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {33 \dfrac {1} {3}} {100} \times 360 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\dfrac {100} {3}} {100} \times 360 \\\\

                                    &= \dfrac {100 \times 360} {3 \times 100} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {100 \times 3 \times 120} {3 \times 100} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {100} \times \cancel 3 \times 120} {\cancel 3 \times \cancel {100}} \\\\
                                    &= 120 \degree
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

What is the area of shape $A$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of shape $A$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Height of the triangle}   &= 2 - 1 \\\\
                                &= 1 \\\\
\text{Base of the triangle}     &= 5 - 2 \\\\
                                &= 3 \\\\
\text{Area of the triangle}     &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{Height of the triangle} \times \text{Base of the triangle} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 1 \times 3 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
\text{Area of the triangle}     &= 2 \times \text{Area of the triangle} \\\\
                                &= 2 \times \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 3} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 3} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                                &= 3
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3$

</div>

\text{Base of the triangle}     &= 5 - 2 \\\\
                                &= 3 \\\\
\text{Area of the triangle}     &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{Height of the triangle} \times \text{Base of the triangle} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 1 \times 3 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
\text{Area of the triangle}     &= 2 \times \text{Area of the triangle} \\\\
                                &= 2 \times \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 3} {2} \\\\

                                &= 3
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What percentage of Mark's counters are blue?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What percentage of Mark's counters are blue?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Percentage of blue in Mark's counter}   &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 100 \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {90 \times 100} {360} \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {90 \times 25 \times 4} {4 \times 90} \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times 25 \times \cancel{4}} {\cancel{4} \times \cancel {90}} \\\\
                                              &= 25 \ \%
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25 \ \%$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Mark has $40$ counters in his bag.

                                              &= 3 \times 10 \\\\
                                              &= 30
\end{aligned}
$

$\dfrac{1}{3}$ of Sarah's counters are red, and the rest are green or blue.

Given that Sarah has $12$ red counters, how many counters are there altogether in her bag?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

\end{aligned}
$

Total number of counters Sarah has $= 36$

**Question**

Sarah has twice as many green counters as blue ones. 

How many blue counters does she have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sarah has twice as many green counters as blue ones. 
<emptyline>
How many blue counters does she have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of blue counters Sarah has $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2a + 12         &= 36 \\\\
3a + 12             &= 36 \\\\
3a                  &= 36 - 12 \\\\
3a                  &= 24 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {3 \times 8} {3} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 8} {\cancel 3} \\\\
a                   &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Number of blue counters Sarah has $= 8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$8$

**Question**

They each pick one counter at random from their own bag.

Who is more likely to pick a green counter?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">They each pick one counter at random from their own bag.
<emptyline>
Who is more likely to pick a green counter?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Probability of picking green counter from Mark's bag}     &= \dfrac {180} {360} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {180} {180 \times 2} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {180}} {\cancel {180} \times 2} \\\\
                                                                &= 0.5 \\\\
\text{Probability of picking green counter from Sarah's bag}    &= \dfrac {8} {36} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {4 \times 2} {4 \times 9} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 2} {\cancel 4 \times 9} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {2} {9} \\\\
                                                                &= 0.22
\end{aligned}
$

Mark is more likely to pick a green counter.
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Mark

**Question**

Sarah measured the temperature of the beaker again $4 \ \text{hours}$ and $30 \ \text{minutes}$ after the last reading on the graph.

At what time did she take this measurement?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>
At what time did she take this measurement?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Time when she took the reading}   &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \ \text{hours} \ 30 \ \text{min} \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \times 60 \ \text{min} + 30 \ \text{min} \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \times 60 + 30 \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 + 240 + 30 \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 + 270 \\\\
                                        &= 3 {:} 20 \ \text{pm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

What percentage of pupils have red as their favourite colour?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What percentage of pupils have red as their favourite colour?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{\% with favourite colour red}   &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 100 \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {90 \times 100} {360} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {90 \times 25 \times 4} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                      &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times 25 \times \cancel 4} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                      &= 25 \ \%
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25 \ \%$

</div>

How many pupils have black as their favourite colour?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many pupils have black as their favourite colour?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Angles around a point add up to} = 360 \degree$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\textNumber of pupils with favourite colour black}        &= \dfrac {360 - 180} {360} \times 180 \\\\
                                                          &= \dfrac {180} {360} \times 180 \\\\
                                                          &= \dfrac {180 \times 180} {360} \\\\
                                                          &= \dfrac {180 \times 2 \times 90} {180 \times 2} \\\\
                                                          &= \dfrac {\cancel {180} \times \cancel 2 \times 90} {\cancel {180} \times \cancel 2} \\\\
                                                          &= 90
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$90$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many hamsters were there in the survey?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many hamsters were there in the survey?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of pets $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {120} {360} \times a     &= 48 \\\\
a                               &= 48 \times \dfrac {360} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {48 \times 360} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {48 \times 120 \times 3} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {48 \times \cancel {120} \times 3} {\cancel {120}} \\\\
a                               &= 48 \times 3 \\\\
a                               &= 144
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of hamsters}       &= \dfrac {60} {360} \times 144 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {60 \times 144} {360} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {60 \times 6 \times 24} {60 \times 6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 6 \times 24} {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 6} \\\\
                                &= 24
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{cats}                             &:& \text{hamsters} \\\\
= & 120 \degree                             &:& 60 \degree \\\\
= & 1                                       &:& \dfrac {60} {120} \\\\
= & 1 \times 48                             &:& \dfrac {60} {120} \times 48 \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {60 \times 48} {120} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {60 \times 2 \times 24} {60 \times 2} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 2 \times 24} {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 2} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& 24
\end{array}
$

Number of hamsters $= 24$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

How many dogs?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many dogs?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using value from the answer above,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of dogs}   &= \dfrac {360 - 120 - 60 - 30} {360} \times 144 \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {150} {360} \times 144 \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {150 \times 144} {360} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \times 30 \times 12 \times 12} {30 \times 12} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel {30} \times \cancel {12} \times 12} {\cancel {30} \times \cancel {12}} \\\\
                        &= 5 \times 12 \\\\
                        &= 60
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{cats}                             &:& \text{dogs} \\\\
= & 120 \degree                             &:& (360 - 120 - 60 - 30) \degree \\\\
= & 120 \degree                             &:& 150 \degree \\\\
= & 1                                       &:& \dfrac {150} {120} \\\\
= & 1 \times 48                             &:& \dfrac {150} {120} \times 48 \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {150 \times 48} {120} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {30 \times 5 \times 4 \times 12} {30 \times 4} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {\cancel {30} \times 5 \times \cancel 4 \times 12} {\cancel {30} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& 5 \times 12 \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& 60
\end{array}
$

Number of dogs $= 60$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Five children took exams in English and Maths.

Their names are Dolly, Holly, Lolly, Molly and Polly.

The bar chart below shows their results.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q37-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q37-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q37-i00.png")

Use the information below to work out which child is represented by each letter.

- Dolly came top in the Maths exam.
- In the English exam, it was Molly who scored the highest.
- Polly got the lowest total score.
- Holly scored $30$ more marks in English than she did in Maths.

</div>

$

                        &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel 4} {\cancel 4} \\\\
                        &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

\begin{aligned}

                                              &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 25} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                              &= 25 \%
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

$18$ people said Edam.

How many people said Goat's Cheese?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$18$ people said Edam.
<emptyline>
How many people said Goat's Cheese?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of people $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times \dfrac {90} {360}    &= 18 \\\\
a                             &= 18 \times \dfrac {360} {90} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {18 \times 360} {90} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {18 \times 90 \times 4} {90} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {18 \times \cancel {90} \times 4} {\cancel {90}} \\\\
a                             &= 18 \times 4 \\\\
a                             &= 72
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of people who said Goat's cheese}    &= \dfrac {30} {360} \times 72 \\\\
                                                  &= \dfrac {30 \times 72} {360} \\\\
                                                  &= \dfrac {5 \times 6 \times 72} {72 \times 5} \\\\
                                                  &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 6 \times \cancel {72}} {\cancel {72} \times \cancel 5} \\\\
                                                  &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

</div>

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{Edam}                                 &:& \text{Goat's} \\\\
= & 90                                          &:& 30 \\\\
= & \dfrac {90} {5}                             &:& \dfrac {30} {5} \\\\
= & \dfrac {18 \times 5} {5}                    &:& \dfrac {6 \times 5} {5} \\\\
= & \dfrac {18 \times \cancel 5} {\cancel 5}    &:& \dfrac {6 \times \cancel 5} {\cancel 5} \\\\
= & 18                                          &:& 6
\end{array}
$

Number of people who said Goat's cheese $= 6$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                    &= \dfrac {5 \times 30 \times 72} {72 \times 5} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 30 \times \cancel {72}} {\cancel {72} \times \cancel 5} \\\\
                    &= 30
\end{aligned}
$

Let the coordinates of E $= (a, b)$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {2a + 7} {2 + 1}       &= 9 \\\\
\dfrac {2a + 7} {3}           &= 9 \\\\
2a + 7                        &= 9 \times 3 \\\\
2a + 7                        &= 27 \\\\
2a                            &= 27 - 7 \\\\
2a                            &= 20 \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {20} {2} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 10} {2} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 10} {\cancel 2} \\\\
a                             &= 10 \\\\
\dfrac {2b + 8} {2 + 1}       &= 4 \\\\
\dfrac {2b + 8} {3}           &= 4 \\\\
2b + 8                        &= 4 \times 3 \\\\
2b + 8                        &= 12 \\\\
2b                            &= 12 - 8 \\\\
2b                            &= 4 \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {4} {2} \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 2} {2} \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
b                             &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (10, 2)$

2a + 7                        &= 27 \\\\
2a                            &= 27 - 7 \\\\

\dfrac {2b + 8} {2 + 1}       &= 4 \\\\

2b + 8                        &= 12 \\\\
2b                            &= 12 - 8 \\\\
2b                            &= 4 \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {4} {2} \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 2} {2} \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
b                             &= 2
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>

![papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q12-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q12-i00.png "papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q12-i00.png")

A point is described by its coordinates, eg point $\text{B}$ on the diagram has coordinates $(9,8)$. This is not the same as $(8,9)$. Point $\text{A}$ has coordinates $(0,0)$.

To move from one point to another on the graph you can travel by $\text{K}$-steps or by $\text{T}$-steps.

A $\text{K}$-step moves you $1$ place to the right and $2$ places up.

A $\text{T}$-step moves you $3$ places to the right and $1$ place up.

</div>

**Question**

Starting from point $\text{A}$, what would your coordinates be after a $\text{K}$-step followed by a $\text{T}$-step?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

                          &= 0 + 1 + 3 \\\\
                          &= 4 \\\\

                          &= 0 + 2 + 1 \\\\
                          &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

$(4, 3)$

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of K step $= a$

Let the number of T step $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 3b    &= 9    &  (1) \\\\
2a + b    &= 8    &  (2)
\end{aligned}
$

Lets subtract equation $2$ from twice of equation $1$ to get the value of b.

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (a + 3b) - (2a + b)      &= 2 \times 9 - 8 \\\\
2a + 6b - 2a - b                  &= 18 - 8 \\\\
2a - 2a + 6b - b                  &= 10 \\\\
5b                                &= 10 \\\\
b                                 &= \dfrac {10} {5} \\\\
b                                 &= \dfrac {5 \times 2} {5} \\\\
b                                 &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 2} {\cancel 5} \\\\
b                                 &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

Lets substitute value of b in equation $1$ to get the value of a.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 3b            &= 9 \\\\
a + 3 \times 2    &= 9 \\\\
a + 6             &= 9 \\\\
a                 &= 9 - 6 \\\\
a                 &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

$3$ K-steps

$2$ T-steps
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$K$-step $=$ $3$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$T$-step $=$ $2$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Megaprint make small business cards with names and contact details on, that people can give to clients as part of their work. The total cost of buying the cards they sell is made up of two amounts.

There is a fixed cost that people must pay no matter how many cards they order and this amount is always the same. Then there is a second amount which depends on the number of cards ordered. These two amounts are added together to give the total cost of the order and the graph below shows what the total cost would be for the number of cards ordered.

**Question**

If $200$ cards are ordered, using the total cost what is the cost of one card?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $200$ cards are ordered, using the total cost what is the cost of one card?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of 1 card}   &= \pounds \dfrac {10} {200} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {10 \times 100} {200} \ \text{p} \\\\\
                        &= \dfrac {10 \times 100} {200} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \times 2 \times 100} {2 \times 100} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel {100}} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {100}} \\\\
                        &= 5 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5 \ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of 1 card excluding fixed charge}    &= \dfrac {7 - 4} {100} \\\\
                                                &= \pounds \dfrac {3} {100} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {3 \times 100} {100} \ \text{p} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {3 \times 100} {100} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {100}} {\cancel {100}} \\\\
                                                &= 3 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of cards $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3} {100} \times a + 4                               &= \dfrac {16 - 6} {500} \times a + 6 \\\\
\dfrac {3a} {100} + 4                                       &= \dfrac {10} {500} \times a + 6 \\\\
\dfrac {3a} {100} + 4                                       &= \dfrac {10a} {500} + 6 \\\\
\dfrac {3a} {100} - \dfrac {10a} {500}                      &= 6 - 4 \\\\
\dfrac {3a \times 5} {100 \times 5} - \dfrac {10a} {500}    &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {15a} {500} - \dfrac {10a} {500}                     &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {15a - 10a} {500}                                    &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {5a} {500}                                           &= 2 \\\\
a                                                           &= 2 \times \dfrac {500} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times 500} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times 5 \times 100} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel 5 \times 100} {\cancel 5} \\\\
a                                                           &= 2 \times 100 \\\\
a                                                           &= 200
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$200$

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

**Question**

The points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are equally spaced.

What are the co-ordinates of the point $B$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are equally spaced.
<emptyline>
What are the co-ordinates of the point $B$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{x-coordinates}    &= \dfrac {0 + 6} {2} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {6} {2} \\\\
                        &= 3 \\\\
\text{y-coordinates}    &= \dfrac {8 + 4} {2} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {12} {2} \\\\
                        &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (3, 6)$
</div>
</div>

**Question**

Make a table of $y$ values (correct to $2$ decimal places) for $x$ values starting at $x = 0$ and going to $x = 5$ in steps of $0.5$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

| Value of $x$ | Value of $y$  |
|--------------|---------------|
|     $0$      | $0$           |
|     $0.5$    | $14.99$       |
|     $1$      | $29.98$       |
|     $1.5$    | $44.86$       |
|     $2$      | $59.41$       |
|     $2.5$    | $73.19$       |
|     $3$      | $85.44$       |
|     $3.5$    | $94.92$       |
|     $4$      | $99.54$       |
|     $4.5$    | $95.49$       |
|     $5$      | $73.25$       |
</div>

<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

| Value of $x$ |                                Value of $y$                                               |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|     $0$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 0 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 0^2) \times (90 + \pi 0^2)} = 0$           |
|     $0.5$    | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 0.5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 0.5^2) \times (90 + \pi 0.5^2)} = 14.99$ |
|     $1$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 1 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 1^2) \times (90 + \pi 1^2)} = 29.98$       |
|     $1.5$    | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 1.5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 1.5^2) \times (90 + \pi 1.5^2)} = 44.86$ |
|     $2$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 2 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 2^2) \times (90 + \pi 2^2)} = 59.41$       |
|     $2.5$    | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 2.5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 2.5^2) \times (90 + \pi 2.5^2)} = 73.19$ |
|     $3$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 3 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 3^2) \times (90 + \pi 3^2)} = 85.44$       |

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the value of $x$ (other than $x = 0$) for which $y = 0$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the value of $x$ (other than $x = 0$) for which $y = 0$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
y               &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0 \times 3      &= x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= \sqrt{x^2} \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= \sqrt{x^2 \times (90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0 ^ 2           &= x^2 \times (90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2) \\\\
0               &= x^2 \times (90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2) \\\\
0               &= 90 - \pi x^2 \\\\
0 + \pi x^2     &= 90 \\\\
\pi x^2         &= 90 \\\\
x^2             &= \dfrac {90} {\pi} \\\\
x               &= \sqrt{\dfrac {90} {\pi}} \\\\
x               &\approx 5.35
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
